title: Asian Paints Ltd - 500820 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Asian Paints Q1 FY27: volume up about 9%, standalone top line up about 17%, PBDIT margin about 22%, with weighted price increase about 7%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a good quarter, with volume growth of about 9% spread across all three months and decorative value growth of about 16.6% on a lower base. Standalone top line grew about 17% and PBDIT, PBT and PAT each grew above 30%, with PBDIT margin about 22%. Consolidated top line grew about 18% and PBDIT margin was about 20.6%, up about 240 bps YoY. Management flagged that material inflation of about 25% is being offset only partly by price increases and that Q2 is seasonally lower-margin, while reiterating a PBDIT margin guidance of 18-20% and a full-year volume band of 8-10%.

Price increases taken in April, May and June

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone PBDIT, PBT and PAT growth

financial_highlights.value: about 45.6% in Q4 FY26 comparison referenced; Q1 margin stated as higher YoY

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16.6% on a lower base; volume growth about 9% overall. Rural and T3/T4 cities grew faster than T1/T2 urban, while B2B urban grew strongly. Kitchen and Weatherseal grew at double digits; White Teak and Bath were weaker.

segments.name: Industrial (PPGAP, Automotive OE)
segments.commentary: Top line up about 13% with PBT up about 5%; PBT margin about 15.7%, down 119 bps. Auto OE, marine and packaging did well; refinishes slow. Management said price increases are deferred for B2B and key accounts.

segments.name: General Industrial
segments.commentary: Growth about 21% but pricing was limited and competition high; PBT margin about 6.9%, lower YoY, with PBT growth about 4%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Growth about 27% with broad-based gains across Egypt, UAE, Nepal and Bangladesh; Ethiopia hit by currency devaluation; Middle East stretched by inflation and demand. PBT margin about 7.9%, up 275 bps.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth band of about 8-10%, held for Q2, Q3 and Q4 given festive season and uncertainty in H2 pricing.
PBDIT margin guidance of 18-20% reiterated; Q2 expected to be seasonally lower-margin on product mix.
Management does not plan further price increases unless volatility becomes alarming in certain categories; a second-half price move could be considered.
Expected pricing impact could be in the range of about 8-9% (vs weighted average about 7%) depending on product mix.
VAM-VAE project Phase 1 to commence by August 2026; VAE to kick off in Q2. Expected to reach near 150,000 MT capacity over about 2-2.5 years.
Management guided that VAE integration could translate into a 300-500 bps gross margin benefit for the relevant category band.
capex_capacity: White cement plant in Fujairah, UAE is complete and fully operational at good capacity utilisation.
VAM-VAE manufacturing ecosystem: first new-generation emulsion plant in India; Phase 1 to commence by August 2026; planned 150,000 MT VAE capacity.
Plant can be controlled from a single control room, per management.
Backward integration cited as a key lever to fund investment and profitable growth and to lower input costs.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 9% with demand described as decent across all three months; management said T1/T2 cities lagged T3/T4 and rural, partly offset by B2B growth in urban markets with government spending.
Some pipeline inventory may have been built ahead of price increases in March to May.
Weighted average price increase about 7%; product-mix-driven differential pricing by category.
Input costs: material inflation about 25%, while some input prices (monomers) have eased and TiO2 turned upward at end-June.
Competitive intensity described as at an all-time high across economy, premium and luxury; discounting more intense in economy segment.
Management estimates Asian Paints grew slightly faster than the industry as smaller players lost share due to supply chain volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 17% share of revenue from new products defined, and where do their margins sit?
qa_highlights.answer: New products are those launched within a three-year window and include emulsions, waterproofing, construction chemicals, premium/luxury and new customer propositions. Management said they support healthy overall margins, but gave no quantified margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Was demand pulled forward by price hikes, and was the Bengal election a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand was decent in all three months and some pipeline inventory came in because of pricing action. T1/T2 growth was weaker than rural, but B2B urban growth compensated. Management said double-digit growth was possible, and the 8-10% band was in line with its expectations.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the volume-value gap about 7% and how much is mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium mix contributed about 3% in the quarter, with economy products still performing well and newer products helping the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crude level at which current price increases keep margins in the 18-20% band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to link margins to crude, citing TiO2 and additives not being crude-linked and weighted-average purchasing. It reiterated 18-20% PBDIT margin guidance as the reference point.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin benefit came from low-cost inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify it in basis points. It said inventory was about 30-45 days, with older low-cost raw material used for about half the quarter, and most of the finished-goods benefit came through in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the VAE project be used only for premium and luxury emulsions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said VAE can be used across categories including economy, adhesives and powders; utilisation depends on product formulation. Ramp-up to near 150,000 MT is expected over about 2-2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 400-500 bps gross margin benefit from VAE still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact bps is hard to pin; the category-level benefit is expected to be in a 300-500 bps band, depending on sourcing advantage and formulation.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation of about 25% versus about 7% price increase; Q2 margin pressure as low-cost inventory fades and raw material bought at higher cost flows through.
Renewed geopolitical conflict and crude-linked volatility affecting freight and key inputs such as TiO2 and monomers.
Competitive intensity described as at an all-time high across all segments; more discounting in economy.
Industrial margins down about 119 bps (PPGAP) and about 120 bps for General Industrial, with industrial price increases deferred.
Home decor (White Teak, Bath) weak; management said the bottom line remains under pressure in that business.
Middle East inflation and demand stress; Ethiopia currency devaluation.
Watch whether H2 price action happens and whether the 8-10% volume band holds through the festive season and into the adverse base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and profit delivery and on the premiumisation and innovation story. Cautious on the outlook, citing volatile raw material prices, competitive intensity and an unknown H2 price path. Evasive on quantifying the low-cost inventory benefit and on any crude-price margin benchmark.
key_quotes: Overall, we are at about a strong 9% volume growth. The growth has been across the months in this entire quarter.

I don't think there is any leeway there. Our whole attempt is that the consumer connect, the emotional marketing, and the technological disruption and innovation are the key points of what we profess as we go forward.
What we can take in, is the point that 18-20% guidance is a good guidance to take.
At the current stage, we are looking at the band of 8-10% for the full FY27.

adds.what: VAM-VAE emulsion plant Phase 1 (planned ~150,000 MT VAE capacity over ~2-2.5 years)

growth.why: FY27 volume guided at 8-10% and held for Q2-Q4, backed by ~7% weighted price increases, demand growth (~9% volume in Q1) and VAM-VAE capacity starting Phase 1 by August 2026, with the PBDIT margin guided at 18-20%; the 9% volume band is a volume guide and the full-year revenue figure is the midpoint, so backing is partial since pricing and volume rely on demand and no hard order book is cited.
